title: Power left in a fibre at 0.2 dB km⁻¹
caption: Loss in decibels adds along the fibre, so the power fraction falls exponentially: 10^(−0.02L). After 10 km 0.63 remains, after 50 km 0.10, and after 100 km the loss is 20 dB: 0.01, only 1%. That is why long links need optical amplifiers.
alt: Graph of the fraction of power received against fibre length from 0 to 120 kilometres: a fall from 1 through 0.63 at 10 km, 0.10 at 50 km and 0.01 at 100 km.
description: The horizontal axis is the fibre length in kilometres; the vertical axis is the fraction of the launched power that arrives.
At 0.2 dB km⁻¹ the loss in dB is 0.2L, and the fraction is 10^(−0.2L/10).
After 10 km: 0.63; 50 km: 0.10 (10 dB); 100 km: 20 dB, or 0.01, 1% of the power.
